extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents), and paralegals handling corrections and disclaimers
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for obtaining certificates of correction, petitions to correct inventorship, correcting assignee names, claiming/repairing priority (35 U.S.C. 119/120/365), and filing statutory or terminal disclaimers under USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 255 Criteria for Certificate of Correction (In re Arnott)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two separate statutory requirements must be met before a certificate of correction for an applicant's mistake may issue: (1) the nature/type of the mistake must be clerical, typographical, or a mistake of minor character; and (2) the proposed correction must not involve changes which would constitute new matter or require reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the above is not satisfied, reissue must be used. Usually, any mistake affecting claim scope must be corrected by reissue. A mistake is not 'minor' if the requested change would materially affect the scope or meaning of the patent. See MPEP § 1412.04 for correction of inventorship via certificate of correction or reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirements for certificates of correction
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee for providing a correction of applicant's mistake, other than inventorship, is set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(a). The fee for correction of inventorship is set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the appropriate fee with the request as required by the cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of assignees' names (PTOL-85B / 37 CFR 3.81 / 1.323 / 1.183)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment data should be completed on the Issue Fee Transmittal Form PTOL-85B (item 3) to comply with 37 CFR 3.81; otherwise the patent will issue to the applicant. A request for a certificate of correction under 37 CFR 1.323 arising from incomplete or erroneous assignee's name furnished in item 3 will not be granted unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 37 CFR 1.183 for correcting assignee name should be directed to the Office of Petitions and include: (A) the petition fee required by 37 CFR 1.17(h); (B) a request that 37 CFR 3.81(a) be waived to permit providing the correct assignee name after issuance; (C) a statement that the failure to include the correct assignee name was inadvertent; and (D) a copy of the Notice of Recordation of Assignment Document.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 256 - Correction of inventorship (statutory standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever through error a person is named in an issued patent as the inventor, or an inventor is omitted, and such error arose without any deceptive intention, the Commissioner may, on application of all parties and assignees with proof, issue a certificate correcting such error. Such error does not invalidate the patent if correctable under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A court before which the matter is called in question may order correction on notice and hearing, and the Commissioner shall issue a certificate accordingly. For effectuating a court order correcting inventorship pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 256, submit a copy of the court order and certificate of correction under 37 CFR 1.323 to the Certificates of Corrections Branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.324 - Petition requirements to correct inventorship in an issued patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to correct inventorship in a patent must be accompanied by: (1) a statement from each person being added and from each person being deleted that the inventorship error occurred without deceptive intention; (2) a statement from the current named inventors who did not submit (1) either agreeing to the change or stating no disagreement; (3) a statement from all assignees agreeing to the change that complies with § 3.73(b); and (4) the fee set forth in § 1.20(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must include the statements and fee required by 37 CFR 1.324(b). The statements in (b)(1) need only contain the required language (e.g., 'The inventorship error ... occurred without any deceptive intention on the part of the applicant.'); the examiner checks for required language only and does not adjudicate deceptive intent. Unlike 37 CFR 1.48(a) for applications, the requirements of 37 CFR 1.324 for patents cannot be waived under 1.183 because statute (35 U.S.C. 256) requires petition of all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of inadvertently-filed 37 CFR 1.48 petitions in issued patents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.48(a) is inadvertently filed in a patent, the petition may be treated as a petition under 37 CFR 1.324, and if grantable, specific form paragraph (10.14) should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 1.324 procedural treatment and form paragraphs when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making standards and disposition forms for 37 CFR 1.324 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs (¶ 10.13–¶ 10.17) provide templates for granting, treating, dismissing, or denying petitions to correct inventorship under 37 CFR 1.324. A petition to correct inventorship requires the specified statements and fee; lack of items leads to dismissal (or denial if insufficient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one or more of the required items is missing, dismissal is appropriate; if items are submitted but insufficient, the petition should be denied (see paragraph 10.17). If deficiency can be cured by a renewed petition, dismissal is appropriate. Provide full explanation of deficiencies when denying. Routing and signature instructions for the internal decision memos are provided in the form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of 37 CFR 1.324 requirements under 37 CFR 1.183
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of rules under 37 CFR 1.183 may be granted for regulatory requirements that are not statutory requirements. Because 35 U.S.C. 256 requires certain things, a petition under 1.183 requesting waiver of statutory requirements of 1.324 is dismissed as moot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petition requests waiver of requirements of 1.324 that are not statutory (e.g., fee, oath/declaration by all inventors), forward to a petitions examiner in the Office of the Deputy Assistant Commissioner for Patent Policy and Projects for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certificate of correction to amend priority claims (35 U.S.C. 119(e) and 120) — conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain conditions, a certificate of correction can be used to correct or add references to prior copending applications for 35 U.S.C. 120 and 119(e) priority or to correct incorrect references pursuant to 37 CFR 1.78(a)(2) and (a)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-365(c) cases: (A) for 120 priority, all requirements in 37 CFR 1.78(a)(1) must have been met in the application which became the patent to be corrected; (B) for 119(e) priority, requirements in 1.78(a)(3) must have been met in the application which became the patent; (C) the prior copending application to be added via the certificate must be identified elsewhere in the application papers (not just first sentence of spec); and (D) it must be clear from the record of the patent and parent application(s) that priority is appropriate. For international-application-based 120/365(c) priority there are analogous conditions plus a requirement to submit documentation showing designation of states and other info. If these conditions are not satisfied, file reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and routing of requests for certificates of correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for certificates of correction should be addressed to the Certificate of Correction Branch, Assistant Commissioner for Patents. Requests will be forwarded to that Branch and listed in a permanent record book. If the patent is involved in an interference, a certificate under 37 CFR 1.324 will not be issued unless a corresponding motion under 37 CFR 1.634 has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of whether an error has been made, responsibility, and whether issuance is justified is made by the Certificate of Correction Branch. Cases may be forwarded for report if necessary. If no certificate issues, notify requester and place correspondence and reports in file. If certificate issues, it will be prepared, forwarded to requester, and supporting docs placed in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and procedural requirements for filing certificate text (PTO-1050 / PTO/SB/44)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are urged to submit the text of the correction on PTO-1050 (or PTO/SB/44). Both parts of PTO-1050 must accompany the request since the second part is placed in the application file for internal use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to use PTO-1050 frequently delays issuance because Office must retype text. Intricate chemical formulas or pages of specification/drawings may be reproduced and mounted on a blank PTO-1050. Use PTO-1050 exclusively regardless of length/complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting conventions and specifics for certificate-of-correction text
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing the correction text, identify exact page and line number of errors (in the printed patent use column and line), conserve space (single-space, begin two lines down), start corrections to each separate column as a sentence, use semicolons to separate corrections within a column, leave two-inch space at bottom of last sheet for attesting officer signature, enclose exact subject matter to be deleted in quotation marks, and enclose subject matter to be added with double hyphens (-- --) except for formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For formulas, set out only the portion to be corrected or paste a photocopy onto PTO-1050. The exact page and line number in the application file should be identified on the request, but on PTO-1050 use column and line number in the printed patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner comments when change in subject matter is involved (PTO-306)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's comments are requested on PTO-306 where, under 37 CFR 1.323, there is a question involving change in subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examiner comments to assist the Certificate of Correction Branch in determining whether the correction would introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory disclaimer requirements (35 U.S.C. 253; 37 CFR 1.321) - content and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory disclaimer to be recorded must be in writing, signed by the patentee or an attorney/agent of record, identify the patent and the complete claim(s) or term being disclaimed (partial-claim disclaimers will be refused), state present extent of patentee's ownership interest, and be accompanied by the fee in § 1.20(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disclaimer filed in an application must be signed by the proper party depending on assignment status (applicant, applicant+assignee if part interest, assignee if entire interest, or attorney/agent). A disclaimer filed in a patent or reexamination must be signed by the patentee (assignee or inventors as appropriate) or attorney/agent of record. Signature need not be original; copies/facsimiles are acceptable per 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee signature and proof-of-ownership requirements for disclaimers (37 CFR 3.73(b) compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an assignee signs the disclaimer, compliance with 37 CFR 3.73(b) is required unless an attorney/agent of record signs. The assignee's ownership interest must be established by filing evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee and specifying where such evidence is recorded in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A submission under 3.73(b) must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee. A 'Certificate Under 37 CFR 3.73(b)' (see MPEP § 324) may be used to comply and may be provided to applicant by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer specifics and limits (37 CFR 1.321(c) and practice in pending applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer (disclaiming all or part of the term) may be filed to overcome double patenting. In pending applications, a terminal disclaimer must be of a terminal portion of the term of the entire patent to be granted (cannot be directed to particular claim(s)); the statute does not provide for conditional disclaimers; the disclaimer should identify the disclaimant and their interest and specify the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filed to obviate a judicially created double patenting rejection, terminal disclaimers must also include provisions that any patent granted shall be enforceable only while commonly owned with the application/patent which formed the basis for the rejection. In pending applications, paralegals process terminal disclaimers: determine compliance with statute/regulations, notify examiner re acceptability, record acceptable disclaimers, and provide data for printing. The paralegal marks the file (green label, stamp, endorsement, PALM entry) and completes a Terminal Disclaimer Informal Memo to notify examiner of informalities; the examiner should inform applicant in next Office action and initial/date the memo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing responsibilities of Certificates of Correction Branch
rubrics_metrics.description: The Certificates of Corrections Branch handles statutory disclaimers filed under 35 U.S.C. 253 and terminal disclaimers (except those filed in an application pending in an Examining Group) including: (A) determining compliance with 35 U.S.C. 253 and 37 CFR 1.321 and 3.73; (B) notifying applicant/patentee when disclaimer is informal; (C) recording the disclaimers; and (D) providing the disclaimer data for printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where terminal disclaimers are filed in an Examining Group application, paralegal of the Office of the Special Program Examiner handles processing and examiner notification as described above.
